full_judgment:
3. The case of the writ-petitioner-respondent Khasru Mia and 38 others was that they formed a Krishi Farming Samabay Samity under the name and style "Gulduba Krishi Farming Co-operative Society Ltd." hereinafter referred to as the Samity within PS-Nabigonj, District-Sylhet now Habigonj in 1974 for mechanized cultivation, The said Samity was registered under the Co-operative Societies Act, on 21-3-1974 vide Regd. No. 2109; that all the aforesaid 39 members of the Samity as landless peasants filed applications to the Sub-Divisional Officer, Habigonj in their individual capacity in separate printed and prescribed form for settlement of a total quantum of land measuring an area of 82.53 acres, each claming 2.50 acres of land appertaining to plot Nos. 651, 652 of Mouza Gulduba. The Sub-Divisional Officer got the matter enquired into by a Magistrate, 1st Class on several occasions and on being satisfied granted permanent settlement of 82.53 acres of land individually in the name of all the 39 members of the Samity each having more or less 2.50 acres of land vide Settlement Case No. 1 of 1975 on 18-10-1975. The said settlement was approved by the ADC (Rev), Sylhet on 10-10-1975. The Sub-Divisional Officer executed 39 permanent deeds of settlement which were registered on 15-11-1975. In the manner, aforesaid petitioner and the other applicants each got 2.13 acres of Government khas land through registered deed of settlement for a period of 15 years with effect from the last of Baishak, 1382 BS (till the 30th Chaitra, 1397 BS) under specific terms and conditions enumerated in the said deed of settlement The aforesaid settlement was made in accordance with the provision of section 81 (1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act The settlement was made heritable after 15 years subject to satisfactory observance of the stipulated terms and conditions. There was a prohibitory condition against alienation before 15 years. 

 4. The further case of the Khasru Mia was that the petitioner paid salami vide DCR dated 17-11-1975 and got delivery of possession on 18-11-1975. The land was mutated in his name in RoR khatian No. 454. The petitioner procured agricultural equipment including tractor for mechanised cultivation of the land. The petitioner brought the land under mechanised cultivation and has been regularly growing crops therein. He paid land revenue vide DCR No. 500731 dated 17-12- 1976. 

 6. On similar assertions and averments, the writ-petitioner-respondents, Rathullah filed Writ Petition No. 443 of 1989 and other writ-petitions also were filed by other individual. The writ respondent-petitioners Ratullah in his writ-petition No. 443 of 1989 impugned the order of cancellation passed by writ-respondent No.1 (petitioner herein). In all the writ-petitions, the leave-petitioner No.1 (writ-respondent No.1) represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms, Government of Bangladesh filed affidavits-in-opposition denying all the assertions and allegations contained in the writ-petition, stating, inter alia, that the Assistant Registrar of Co-operative Society by order dated 20-7-1988 cancelled the registration of the petitioners samity as the said samity ceased to have any activities of a co-operative societies; that the petitioners failed to bring the demised land under cultivation and that they violated the terms and conditions of the deed of settlement; that many of the members of the so-called samity were not even aware of any settlement made in their favour; that some of the alleged members are residents of foreign countries and Khasru Mia unauthorisedly used their names; that the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Nabigongj has already started Resumption Case No.1 of 1987-88; that after careful consideration of the inquiry report pursuant to application filed by the petitioners against the said Resumption Case, the Government vacated the order of stay, granted earlier and cancelled settlements made in favour of the petitioners as the samity had no existence; that the Government directed the District Administration to implement the Government policy towards the establishment of cluster village. The writ-petitioner- respondent in reply to the affidavit-in-opposition filed affidavit-in-reply, reiterating the assertions made in the writ-petitions. They further stated that the settlement was not dependent on the formation of any co-operative society and that the society was not cancelled in accordance with the Rules. The writ-petitioner-respondents by filing supplementary affidavit also stated that although the lease in their favour was granted initially for a period of 15 years with effect from 1st Baishak, 1382 BS i.e. till the 30th of Chaitra, 1397 BS but before the expiry of the said lease period respondent No.4 on 27-3-1989 arbitrarily and illegally cancelled the said settlement without serving any show cause notice upon them. The petitioners further contended that on 20-8-1990 (before the expiry of the settlement) they approached the concerned authority for extension of the period of settlement by filing application to that effect and respondent No. 3 received the same on the day but refrained from doing anything on the plea that in the meantime the High Court Division has granted an order of stay. Copy of the application seeking extension of the period of settlement was annexed and marked as Annexure-X. It was further contended that during the recent survey operation the petitioners were found to be in physical possession of the demised land and accordingly, the record of right has been prepared in their names in the face of objection raised by respondent No. 3 (Deputy Commissioner, Habigonj). 

 9. Mr Fida M Kamal, the learned Additional Attorney-General appearing for the petitioners, contended that the writ-petitioner-respondents, Khasru Mia and Ratullah having failed to prove that the demise land under cultivation belonged to them and having violated the terms and conditions of the deed of settlement, the High Court Division committed an error of law in making the Rule absolute. He further contended that the writ- petitioner-respondents having unauthorisedly using the name of many members of the society although some of the members are the residents of foreign countries and some of the writ-petitioners did not even know about the alleged settlement and the High Court Division having failed to notice this aspect, committed an error of law in making the Rule absolute. 

 11. We have heard and considered the submissions. On perusal of the impugned judgment, we find that learned Judges of the High Court Division having meticulously considered the case of the parities, the provisions of Co-operative Societies Ordinance, 1984 and also considered the decisions of the superior Court and thus came to the finding that the settlements granted in favour of the writ- petitioner respondent Khasru Mia and Ratullah along with others were cancelled without giving them any notice to show cause for alleged infringement of the terms and conditions of such a lease. Admittedly, the writ-petitioner-respondents were granted settlement by the writ petition respondent No.1 by registered instrument and as such the writ petitioners were legally entitled to be heard before any cancellation of the settlement for the alleged violation of terms and conditions of the lease deed. In the instant case, we find that the learned Judges of the High Court Division upon meticulous consideration as well as on the basis of materials on record held that no prior notice was given to the writ-petitioners and along with others before cancellation of the registered deed of settlement. We are fully in agreement with the findings and decisions arrived at by the High Court Division. For all the above reasons, we find no substance in these two petitions. Accordingly, these are dismissed.
